note: RFC 7296 Section 2.7 (rfc/full/rfc7296.txt): "The responder MUST accept a single proposal or reject them all and return an error. The error is given in a notification of type NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN." and "The accepted cryptographic suite MUST contain exactly one transform of each type included in the proposal." NegotiateIKE picks one proposal or returns ErrNoProposalChosen (TestProposalNegotiationFirstMatch/NoMatch); TestEsnResponderAnswersOnlyAValueTheOfferCarried asserts SAr2 carries one proposal with exactly one ESN transform of a value the offer carried and maps refusal to NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN. Interop: checkESNExtendedOnlyRefused isolates the ESN type (aes256gcm16-esn alone) and asserts ze reached NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN (logged by buildChildlessAuthResponse as it builds the refusal notify) with no CHILD_SA on strongSwan and zero XFRM states on both ends, recorded red with the espProposalMatches ESN comparison reverted; checkESNBothOffered asserts both ends keyed, strongSwan's state carries no esn, and traffic crosses, so both ends selected the same single ESN value. Limitation, not a defect: the interop negative reads ze's log, not strongSwan's receipt of the notify; the wire mapping is held by the engine unit test. Re-judged 2026-10-10 (independent judge, mode rejudge): every tagged unit, and the helpers they call (waitLog, listSAs, checkXFRMCount, establish, waitXFRM, xfrmState, verifyTunnelTraffic), is byte-identical between 35c3b0b699 and HEAD; the diff touches the scenarioCheckers registry shape (both ESN scenarios still map to these checkers) and the childless-IKE-SA checkers, and the producer change adds only a fix field to the refusal log line, so the verdict stands.
